statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum length (number of nodes) of a valid path in the tree. A valid path is a sequence of distinct nodes v_0, ..., v_{k-1} (k >= 1) such that for every i with 0 <= i < k-1, v_i and v_{i+1} are adjacent in the tree (i.e., v_i = parent[v_{i+1}] or v_{i+1} = parent[v_i]) and s[v_i] != s[v_{i+1}]. The length of such a path is k.
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: The function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail, overflow, panic, or go out of bounds).
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, we have 1 <= r <= n.
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: For every valid path (as defined in spec_1) of length k, we have k <= r.
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: There exist nodes u and v with 0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n such that the unique simple path between u and v in the tree is a valid path (as defined in spec_1) and has exactly r nodes.
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: If every edge in the tree connects nodes with different characters, then the function returns r equal to the maximum number of nodes on any simple path in the tree (i.e., the tree diameter in nodes). Equivalently, r = 1 + max_{u,v in [0,n)} dist(u,v), where dist(u,v) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between u and v.
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122); and for every i with 1 <= i < n, s[i] != s[parent[i]].

statement: Whenever the function returns ok r, r is the maximum, over all pairs (a, b) with 0 <= a <= b < n and, for every k with a <= k < b, s[k] != s[k+1], of the number of nodes b - a + 1 in that interval.
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122); and for every i with 1 <= i < n, parent[i] = i-1 (so the tree is a path 0-1-2-...-(n-1)).

statement: If the tree is a star with center 0, then: if there exist two distinct indices i, j with 1 <= i < n, 1 <= j < n, i != j, such that s[i] != s[0] and s[j] != s[0], then r = 3; else if there exists an index i with 1 <= i < n such that s[i] != s[0], then r = 2; else r = 1.

statement: The function returns r = 1 if and only if for every i with 1 <= i < n, s[i] = s[parent[i]]. Equivalently, r >= 2 if and only if there exists an index i with 1 <= i < n such that s[i] != s[parent[i]].

statement: The function returns the same result when called with (parent, s) and with (parent', s'). That is, longest_path(parent, s) = longest_path(parent', s').
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122). Let parent' be an array of length n with parent'[0] = -1 and for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent'[i] < n, such that parent' defines a tree rooted at 0. Let s' be an array of length n with lowercase English letters. Suppose there exists a bijection f: [0,n) -> [0,n) such that f(0) = 0, for every i with 1 <= i < n the unordered pair {f(i), f(parent[i])} is an edge in the tree defined by parent' (i.e., f(i) = parent'[f(parent[i])] or f(parent[i]) = parent'[f(i)]), and s[i] = s'[f(i)] for all i.

n = len(parent) = len(s); n >= 1; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n and following parent pointers from i eventually reaches 0 (so parent defines a tree rooted at 0); for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122). Let parent' be an array of length n+1 such that parent'[i] = parent[i] for 0 <= i < n, and parent'[n] = j for some j with 0 <= j < n. Let s' be an array of length n+1 such that s'[i] = s[i] for 0 <= i < n, and s'[n] = s[j]. Then parent' defines a tree rooted at 0 (with n+1 nodes) and s' consists of lowercase English letters.

statement: longest_path(parent', s') is either longest_path(parent, s) or longest_path(parent, s) + 1.

Let parent' be an array of length n+1 such that parent'[i] = parent[i] for 0 <= i < n, and parent'[n] = j for some j with 0 <= j < n. Let s' be an array of length n+1 such that s'[i] = s[i] for 0 <= i < n, and s'[n] = c where c is a lowercase English letter and c != s[j]. Then parent' defines a tree rooted at 0 (with n+1 nodes) and s' consists of lowercase English letters.
